purpose: Selection grid: the same machines re-arranged (one 7-8 tie circuit out, a new load at the device's HV bus, different dispatch and voltage schedule). Held-out runs only; the solver never sees it, and its score is the one the RSI accept rule uses.

case.name: grid_B
case.description: Kundur two-area re-arranged: device in GENROU 3's slot; one of the three 7-8 tie circuits (Line_6) out of service; a new 200 MW load PQ_3 at the device's HV bus 9; 150 MW load PQ_2 at bus 10; loads moved from bus 8 to bus 7; device at 720 MW (above any training dispatch) with a 1.02 pu voltage schedule

device_under_test.params_note: ANDES inputs from medium_kundur_regf1/holdout/answer_key.json (seed 0): six parameters scaled by U[0.7, 1.3]; wdrp and Qdrp are converter-base droops x Sb/Sn (ANDES applies them to system-base P and Q); KPv = 6 for damping of the 0.85 Hz mode. The same device sits in every grid.

design_notes: The device's loading decides whether a voltage-loop error is visible at all. At 550 MW a 30% error in the voltage-loop gain KPv cost 0.02 to 0.06 on a line trip, at 700 MW 0.16 to 0.22, and at grid A's op1 it saturates. 720 MW keeps that error visible without saturating and sits just above the training dispatch.
